candidates.original_title: The microRNA miR-34a inhibits prostate cancer stem cells and metastasis by directly repressing CD44
candidates.description: miR-34a is underexpressed in CD44+ LAPC4 cells relative to CD44- LAPC4 cells
candidates.citation_sentence: This experiment is comparable to what was reported in Figure 1B of Liu et al. (2011) and described in Protocol 3 in the Registered Report (Li et al., 2015).
candidates.notes: The replication found miR-34a was elevated at 202% in CD44+ cells (opposite direction from the original's 3.4%). The gating strategy was changed from top 10% to top 1% due to weak CD44 signal. Let-7b was in the same direction as the original, but miR-34a was not. candidates.original_title: The microRNA miR-34a inhibits prostate cancer stem cells and metastasis by directly repressing CD44
candidates.description: Expression of miR-34a inhibits tumor regeneration of LAPC4 cells in NOD/SCID mice
candidates.citation_sentence: This experiment is similar to what was reported in Supplemental Figure 5C of Liu et al. (2011) and described in Protocol 4 in the Registered Report (Li et al., 2015).
candidates.notes: The original reported miR-34a inhibited tumor regeneration (0.15g vs 0.54g control at 69 days). The replication found similar tumor weights between miR-34a transduced and control groups (0.55g vs 0.51g at 100 days), not statistically significant (t(18)=0.432, p=0.671). The original used n=6; replication used n=7. [ling26: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: The microRNA miR-34a inhibits prostate cancer stem cells and metastasis by directly repressing CD44
candidates.description: CD44 expression is inversely correlated with miR-34a expression in tumors from DU145 cells transduced with miR-34a
candidates.citation_sentence: This experiment was described in Protocol 5 in the Registered Report (Li et al., 2015) and is conceptually similar to what was reported in Figure 4A of Liu et al. (2011), which used DU145 cells transduced with a retroviral vector encoding miR-34a.
candidates.notes: The replication used LAPC4 cells with lentiviral vectors instead of DU145 cells with retroviral vectors. Critically, miR-34a was not detectable in tumors from miR-34a transduced LAPC4 cells in vivo (likely silenced), so the CD44 result cannot be interpreted as a direct test of the original claim. The authors note this complicates interpretation. [ling26: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: The microRNA miR-34a inhibits prostate cancer stem cells and metastasis by directly repressing CD44
candidates.description: miR-34a directly represses CD44 through binding sites in the 3'UTR of CD44, as measured by luciferase reporter assay
candidates.citation_sentence: This is similar to what was reported in Figure 4D of Liu et al. (2011) and described in Protocol 7 in the Registered Report (Li et al., 2015).
candidates.notes: The original reported decreased luciferase signal with wild-type reporter + miR-34a oligos (0.67 vs 1.00), partially abrogated with double mutant (0.78 vs 1.00). The replication found no significant difference (0.99 vs 1.00 for wild-type; 1.19 vs 1.00 for double mutant). Only the double mutant was tested in the replication, not individual binding sites. [ling26: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: The microRNA miR-34a inhibits prostate cancer stem cells and metastasis by directly repressing CD44
candidates.description: The original study claimed that let-7b expression was reduced in CD44-positive LAPC4 prostate cancer stem cells relative to CD44-negative cells; this replication tested the claim using FACS-sorted LAPC4 cells.
candidates.citation_sentence: This experiment is comparable to what was reported in Figure 1B of Liu et al. (2011) and described in Protocol 3 in the Registered Report (Li et al., 2015).
candidates.notes: The replication found let-7b underexpressed in CD44-positive cells, in the same direction as the original. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: The microRNA miR-34a inhibits prostate cancer stem cells and metastasis by directly repressing CD44
candidates.description: The original study claimed that miR-34a expression was reduced in CD44-positive LAPC4 prostate cancer stem cells relative to CD44-negative cells; this replication tested the claim using FACS-sorted LAPC4 cells.
candidates.citation_sentence: This experiment is comparable to what was reported in Figure 1B of Liu et al. (2011) and described in Protocol 3 in the Registered Report (Li et al., 2015).
candidates.notes: The replication found miR-34a elevated rather than reduced in CD44-positive cells. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: The microRNA miR-34a inhibits prostate cancer stem cells and metastasis by directly repressing CD44
candidates.description: The original study claimed that enforced miR-34a expression inhibited tumor regeneration and reduced LAPC4 xenograft tumor growth; this replication tested the claim by comparing miR-34a-transduced, negative-control-transduced, and untransduced LAPC4 cells in mice.
candidates.citation_sentence: This experiment is similar to what was reported in Supplemental Figure 5C of Liu et al. (2011) and described in Protocol 4 in the Registered Report (Li et al., 2015).
candidates.notes: The replication found similar tumor weights and growth profiles across groups, with no statistically significant effect of miR-34a. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: The microRNA miR-34a inhibits prostate cancer stem cells and metastasis by directly repressing CD44
candidates.description: The original study claimed that residual LAPC4 tumors showed no or only a marginal increase in miR-34a expression after miR-34a manipulation; this replication tested miR-34a expression in tumors derived from miR-34a-transduced LAPC4 cells.
candidates.citation_sentence: The original study reported no, or marginal (~3X), increases in miR-34a expression in the residual tumors formed from prostate cancer cells, specifically LAPC4, LAPC9, and DU145, transiently transfected with miR-34a oligo compared to vector control (Liu et al., 2011).
candidates.notes: No miR-34a was detected in tumors derived from miR-34a-transduced cells, but the authors noted that in vivo silencing prevented clear interpretation of the intended overexpression comparison. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: The microRNA miR-34a inhibits prostate cancer stem cells and metastasis by directly repressing CD44
candidates.description: The original study claimed that CD44 expression was inversely correlated with miR-34a expression in tumors formed from miR-34a-transduced prostate cancer cells; this replication measured CD44 expression in tumors derived from miR-34a-transduced LAPC4 cells.
candidates.citation_sentence: This experiment was described in Protocol 5 in the Registered Report (Li et al., 2015) and is conceptually similar to what was reported in Figure 4A of Liu et al. (2011), which used DU145 cells transduced with a retroviral vector encoding miR-34a.
candidates.notes: CD44 expression did not differ between groups, but interpretation was limited because miR-34a was not detectable in the miR-34a-transduced tumors. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: The microRNA miR-34a inhibits prostate cancer stem cells and metastasis by directly repressing CD44
candidates.description: The original study claimed that miR-34a directly repressed CD44 through putative miR-34a binding sites in the CD44 3-prime UTR; this replication tested wild-type and double-mutant CD44 3-prime UTR luciferase reporters in DU145 cells.
candidates.citation_sentence: This is similar to what was reported in Figure 4D of Liu et al. (2011) and described in Protocol 7 in the Registered Report (Li et al., 2015).
candidates.notes: The replication found no significant miR-34a effect on the wild-type reporter and described the results as not consistent in direction with the original study. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]
